source_title: Request for Proposals for Professional Services for Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) 2055

requirements.requirement: Questions are due September 16, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. ET.
Proposal packages are due October 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
Anticipated performance begins around January 1, 2027 and final handoff is due no later than December 31, 2028.
The total not-to-exceed budget is $215,000, with base scope distinguished from optional or additive services.
The MTP and development process must comply with applicable federal and state metropolitan transportation planning requirements, including 23 CFR 450 Subpart C.
The consultant must designate a project manager, maintain a work plan and schedule, attend coordination and milestone meetings, invoice monthly, and apply QA/QC.
Engagement must be integrated into technical tasks and tied to identified decisions, information needs, participants, methods, timing, analysis, communication, and use of findings.
The consultant must adapt and administer a statistically valid regional survey, explaining sampling, weighting, representativeness, specialized partners, findings, and limitations.
Regional conditions analysis must focus on findings that influence plan decisions, investment strategy, performance measures, or recommendations rather than reproduce descriptive information.
The consultant must refine vision, goals, objectives, KPIs, and the required system performance report using maintainable and understandable measures.
The consultant must integrate updated population, employment, land-use, scenario, and travel-model assumptions while accounting for the staged availability of updated ITDM outputs.
The consultant must support resource-allocation goals, improve project scoring, run a project call, quality-control data, assign scores, incorporate ITDM outputs, and support fiscal constraint.
Major recommendations must state outcomes, roles, mechanisms, time horizon, dependencies, funding or staffing implications, and monitoring method.
Final public documents must be accessible and concise, with native/editable report files plus native mapping files and scripts for future amendments.
The main qualifications response is limited to 16 pages; listed forms, addendum, cover page, table of contents, vendor-profile information, and separate quote are excluded.

The counted response includes a one-page cover letter, one-to-two-page firm overview, one-to-four-page approach, maximum two-page team section, maximum three-page project sheets, and maximum four-page resumes.
At least three relevant project examples must identify client, participating staff, and staff roles; IMPO experience may be listed but IMPO references are prohibited.
Forms A, B, and C must be completed; Form A requests legal organization type, professional liability status, vendor number, and SAM.gov UEI.
Vendors must monitor the official procurement page for addenda through the due date, sign the questions addendum, and include it in the response.
A separate quote PDF must provide costs, rates, and hours of key staff by major task.
Evaluation weights are project approach 35 points, project team 35 points, and past project experience/examples 30 points.
The procurement uses FHWA and FTA federal planning funds and requires current federal certifications and Title VI assurances.
The vendor warrants that submission information is true and accurate, that it can supply the work, and that delegation beyond disclosed subcontracting requires prior written permission.

The sample contract lists general liability, auto liability, umbrella liability, workers compensation, and employer liability thresholds, but also contains an alternative no-insurance clause by agreement of all parties.
Pre-existing works remain with the contractor only if listed as pre-existing works in the agreement; delivery planning must identify tools, methods, code, data, and licenses accurately.
